FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
The secondary educational-document list includes a yearbook photograph, school records, or at least two report cards from different years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
An original or certified professional degree or license, or a driver-education certificate, may serve as secondary documentation in the guide. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
The guide lists a Medicare or Medicaid card and a medical-eligibility card among secondary documents. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
Secondary-document examples include original adoption papers, a baptismal certificate, and a Louisiana property deed or title, including a burial plot. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
A vehicle registration, a vehicle title in the applicant’s name, or a motor-vehicle lien document appears in the secondary-document list. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
A utility statement showing the applicant’s name and address, or a receipt showing that utilities were activated, may be secondary documentation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
The guide’s secondary-document list includes health, home, life or automobile insurance policies. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
A printed payroll stub or wage-and-tax forms covering two years are listed as secondary documents. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
The secondary-document list includes prison-release papers, a probation-officer letter, or verification from a state agency responsible for placing a deprived or impaired person. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
Initial REAL ID issuance requires evidence of identity, lawful United States status, birth date and Social Security number, plus at least two documents showing the principal home address. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A01
A graduated learner permit limits driving to supervision by a fully licensed driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A01
The guide connects the higher crash risk of teenage drivers with limited driving experience and immaturity. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
Louisiana graduated licensing proceeds from a supervised learner permit to a restricted intermediate license and then a full license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
The first graduated-licensing stage requires an applicant to be at least fifteen. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
The learner stage requires thirty classroom hours and eight hours of behind-the-wheel instruction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
The learner-stage applicant must pass the vision and knowledge examinations. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
A learner-stage driver must be accompanied by a licensed adult aged at least twenty-one or a sibling aged at least eighteen [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
Advancement from learner to intermediate requires holding the learner license at least 180 days and reaching the sixteenth birthday. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A02
For a sixteen-year-old’s intermediate upgrade, a parent or legal guardian must attest to at least fifty driving-practice hours with a licensed parent, guardian or adult aged at least twenty-one, including fifteen hours at night. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A02
The intermediate stage requires completing the learner stage and being at least sixteen. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A02
The guide requires a road-skills score of at least eighty percent for intermediate licensing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A02
An intermediate driver may not drive from eleven p.m. to five a.m. without a licensed adult aged at least twenty-one or a sibling aged at least eighteen [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A02
From six p.m. to five a.m., an intermediate driver may carry no more than one passenger younger than twenty-one who is outside the immediate family. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A02
The intermediate license must be maintained until the driver turns seventeen. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A02
A full license follows successful completion of the learner and intermediate stages, or a first application made at age seventeen or older. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A02
An applicant aged eighteen or older who has not entered graduated licensing may apply for a full Class E license or learner permit after a thirty-eight-hour driver-education course, or a six-hour pre-licensing course plus eight driving-instruction hours. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A02
A vehicle used on Louisiana highways must have liability insurance or another legally allowable substitute. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A02
At license issuance, an applicant must provide insurance evidence for vehicles the applicant owns. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A02
Acceptable insurance proof identifies the insurer, policy number, coverage dates, vehicle, insured person and insurer’s NAIC number. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A02
The insurance card must remain in the vehicle as evidence of coverage. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A03
A driver-license application may involve vision screening, a traffic-law knowledge test and an on-road skills test. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A03
Vision is screened when a person applies for or renews a driver license or learner permit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A03
The licensing vision screening is not a medical examination. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A03
The guide states a minimum vision standard of 20/40 for safe driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A03
A person who fails the vision screening receives a report for a vision specialist to complete. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A03
When corrective lenses are needed to pass vision screening, the license requires wearing them while driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A03
The corrective-lens restriction is displayed as code 01 on the license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A03
After laser correction, removing the lens restriction requires visiting OMV and passing screening without glasses or contact lenses. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A03
Every first-time applicant must pass a knowledge test covering signs, signals, safe driving and Louisiana driving laws. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A03
The knowledge examination uses multiple-choice questions drawn from the guide’s information. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A03
Most offices administer the knowledge examination on a computer. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F42 | anchor: A03
A correct-answer rate of eighty percent is required to pass the knowledge examination. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F43 | anchor: A03
Proper identification is required whenever the knowledge examination is taken. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F44 | anchor: A03
The guide advises reading the manual at least three times before the written examination. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F45 | anchor: A03
The guide advises reading the whole question and all answer choices before selecting an answer. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F46 | anchor: A03
The guide recommends arriving at least one hour before the office’s final testing time. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]
